sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Drowsy, dulness of the head. Indisposed 1o
thinking, early in the morning, with a feeling ol warmth
in the face and hot furehead. {Stupefaction and heaviness
of the head, in the morning, as after intoxication. Dizzy,
in the morning. The head feels gloomy, and heavy, he
forgets what he is about to do or say. Vertigo, the head
is affeclc^, (immediately.) Vertigo and slight obtusion of
the head. Staggering gait, without vertigo. Headache
in the morning, as from nightly revelling. Heaviness of
the head, (a- 2 h ) Feeling ol heaviness and aching pain
in the forehead, (1. d.) Continual heaviness and pain
over the whole head, (1. 2. d.) Obtusion ai.d throbbing
in the forehead, (9. d.) Headache in the left temple and
forehead, with vertigo, reeling, staggering, and anxiety
with sweat. The vertex feels bruised and sensitive, (2.
d.) Headache after dinner, (21. d.) Headache in the
top of the head, in the morning when rising, for 5 days.
Headache above the eyebrows, after the moderate use of
veal. Headache, when waking, fulness in the abdomen,
diarrhoea with chilliness. Pressure in the fore-part of the
head, as if the eyes would start from their sockets, and
as if thev were surrounded by little stones. Violent
aching pain deep in the head, behind the left eye, (a. 10
h.) Aching pain in the right temple. Pressure on the
top of the head, as if a slone were pressing upon it, (7. d.)
Pressure on the top of the head, worse when laying the
hand upon it, (3. d.) Violent pressing together in the
occiput, ihe parts becoming stiff ; afterwards pain in the
nape of the neck, as if the hairs were pulled at, extending
down to the shoulders, with tension and stitches over the
face and neck, with diminished deglutition, anxiety, and
arrest of breathing, from 11 o'clock in the forenoon until
4 o'clock in the afternoon, (3. 4. d.) The headache be-

NITRUM NITIUTE OF POTASH.

came almost intolerable when stooping. She was unable to
eat, on account of headache, (27. d ) During the headache
the eyelids become closed. The aching in ihe occiput
is diminished by lying the hair up. Tbe headache and
pain in the neck last from evening till morning, and the
day following ; the left side especially is affected. Painful
pressure towards the occiput, gradually changing to stitch-
ing, increased by contact, and felt even when in a state
of rest at regular intervals. Frequent feeling of pressure
and heaviness in the occiput, (13. d.) Aching pain in
the head, in the evening, (14. d.) Headache, especially
in the afternoon, (12. d) Pressure, with tearing, in the
right side of the forehead, behind the eye, towards the
occiput, worse after coffee, when walking, stitching at
regular intervals ; abating when driving in the open air.
Tensive pain deep in the head, after dinner. Pain in the
head, distensive, with stitches in the left ear and the
clavicles, whence the pain extended into the elbows, (22.
d-) Contractive pain in the forehead and eyes, terminating
in the tip of the nose as a griping pain. Contractive pain
in the vertex for two hours. Drawing and tearing in the
occiput, she was unable to move the head, with stiffness
of the nape of the neck, for one hour ; in two hours draw-
ing and tearing in the scapulae, with great weakness of the
body ; she was scarcely able to move her feet ; at the
same time coldness without thirst, in the night heat with-
out thirst, without any subsequent sweat, (6. d.) Tearing
in the right temple, from evening till morning, relieved by
pressing upon the parts, (30. d.) Tearing in the left
temple, from time to lime, (8. d.) Stitching and pressing
asunder in the left side of the forehead, when stooping.
Stitching pain in the forehead behind the eyes, at regular
intervals, worst when walking ; single stitches in long
pauses when at rest, the whole afternoon and evening.
Stinging in the left temple,' immediately after dinner, (15.
d.) Single stitches in the left side of the vertex. Violent
stitch in the left side of the occiput, during the menses,
(a. 29 d.) Feeling of looseness and stitches in the brain.
Hacking and stitching in the head, with pressure around
the eyes, and drowsiness, with increase of the pains.
Headache, on the top of the head, as if the hairs were

1

NITRUM — NITRATE OF POTASH.

pulled upon. Pain at one place on the right side and
near the vertex, as if the scalp were contracted, early in
the morning after rising. Jerking pain in the occiput,
apparently in the bone, in three quarters of an hour in the
hip-bone, where it disappeared in a few hours and was
succeeded by a tensive pain behind the right car, con-
tinuing the whole night. Burning throbbing on the left
side of the occiput, in the evening when in bed. Rush of
blood to the head, (a. 20 m.) Great sensitiveness of the
scalp, it is painful to the touch, (a. 5 d.) Great falling off
of the hair, (a. 30 d.) Small scurfy places on the hairy
scalp, with itching, (a. 25 d.) Many pimples on the nape
of the neck and occiput, disappearing again the next day,
(a. 30 d.)

sections.label: Eyes
sections.text:
Painful pressure in the eyes, as if sand or dust
had got in, (a. 16 d.) Pressure in the left eye, under the
upper lid, as of a hair. Violent itching of the upper
margins of both orbits, frequently, (4. d.) Itching of the
right eye, and continual secretion of acrid tears. Burning
smarting, especially of the left eye, as if salt-water had
got in, (28. d.) Burning smarting in the right lids ; he is
obliged to rub. Violent burning of the eyes, with redness
of the canthi, for three days. Burning and lachrymation,
in the morning, (22. d.) Involuntary lachrymation of the
right eye. Continual tearing of the inner canlhi. Aggluti-
nation of the right eye, in the morning, (19. d.) Coloured
wheels before the eyes, the sight being very good, for two
days. Rainbow-like circle around the light, in the evening.
Transitory blindness. After taking the Nitrum, the smell
of camphor frequently obscured her sight.

sections.label: Ears
sections.text:
Pain in the ears, a tension. Tearing in the
right meatus auditorius, (7. d.) Stitching in the right ear,
she was unable to lie upon it in the night, (34. d.) Dull
stitching pain in the right ear.- Stitching in the ear, with
headache, (:15. d.) Tingling in the ears (immediately,)
(also 37 d.) Continual deafness. Violent itching in the
internal meatus auditorius, (15. d.) Inflammation and
swelling of the right lobule, with violent burning and
jerking. Tensive pain behind the right ear, the whole day,
with switching when the pain decreases. Tearing behind
the ears, for two hours, (14. d.) Violent stitches behind

NITRUJI — NITRATE OF POTASH.

the left, ear, towards the joint of the jaw. Stitching behind
the right ear, apparently deep in the head.

sections.label: Nose
sections.text:
Feeling of swelling in the right nostril, it is
painful to the touch. Sore fain of the right nostril, high
up, with sensitiveness to external pressure. Burning in
the right nostril, as if sore, when blowing the nose, (a. 4
d.) Ulcer deep in the right nostril, becoming covered
with a scurf in a few days, (a. 19 d.) The little scab at
the tip of the nose begins to bleed ; next, day the nose
bleeds without the head being relieved. Bleeding of the
nose, three times a week ; the blood was acrid like vine-
gar, (a. 20 d.) Bleeding of the nose, in the afternoon, (a.
20 d.) When blowing the nose, coagulated blood is ex-
pelled from it, (a. 17 d.) Itching of the right side of the
nose, and afterwaids fine stinging of the lip of the nose,
towards evening, (5. d.) Itching and tingling of the lip
of the nose, (22. d.) Pustule on the left side of the nose,
tensive and painful. Griping and burning around the
wings of the nose. Pain of the tip of the nose, as if a
pustule would form upon it, (6. d.) Burning of the nose,
round about, with digging-up and griping, increased by
contact, with swelling of the right nostril, as if an eruption
had formed in it, with wmt of air. The nasal bones are
painful, especially when touching them. The skin of the
nose is red as if inflamed. The tip of the nose is inflamed,

Face — Tensive pain in the cheeks, with redness of the
same, increased throbbing in the head, apparently in the
middle of the brain. Tearing in the zygomata. Tearing
in the facial bones of the left side. Tearing, first in the
right si le of the chin, afterwards below the outer right
rna'leolus when silting. Prickings in the left cheek, after-
wards burning, (38. d.) Gnawing pain in the left upper
jaw, close to the wing of the nose, (5. d.) Jerking pain
in the right zygoma, in the night. Jerking, intermittent
pain in the zygoma, towards ihe vertex, the whole day,
sometimes also in the wrist-joint. Jerking pain in the up-
per jaw and the zygomata. Pale countenance, as after a
long disease. Frequent, violent itching of the face. A
wart on the left cheek becomes larger and itching.

Jaws and Teeth. — Vesicles on the upper lip, with in-

6

NITRUM — NITRATE OF POTASH.

flamed circumference and tensive pain, (a. 16 h) Pres-
sure and dull stiicliing in the right articulation of the jaw,
during motion and deglutition, (5. d.) Tearing in the left
jaw extending into the head, wilh toothache on the same
side, relieved by pressure and by lying upon the part, in
the evening when in bed. Toothache, drawing and stitch-
ing, now on the right, now on the left side, in the upper
molar teeth, in the open air as well as in the room. Jerk-
ing toothache in the left upper row, like an ulcer. Tear-
ing toothache, with tearing in the head, from morning till
noon. Stitches in a hollow tooth when touching it, the
gums being swollen, inflamed, red, painful, readily bleed-
ing. Boring toothache, with pressure in the head, and al-
ternate heat and coldness, towards noon ; relieved in the
evening. Ulcerative pain in the upper, especially the hind
teeth, (8. d.) She is waked from sleep at 3 o'clock in the
morning, and at midnight, by a throbbing toothache, ag-
gravated by cold, uninfluenced by warm things. Sensation
in an upper carious molar tooth, as if the air were entering
and rushing out again. Jerking pains in the teeth, (S. d.)
The toothache becomes more violent by the air entering
the tooth, and extends even as far as the incisor teeth.
Swelling of the gums outer and inner, of the right upper
jaw, scorbutic condition.

Mouth- — Burning of the tip and anterior surface of the
tongue, as if wounded, (cut,) in the evening, (15. 16- d.)
Small, burning pimples on ihe tip of the tongue, increas-
ing in the evening, (a. 14 d.) Burning blister on the lip
of the tongue, (a. 18 d.) Tongue coated with while mu-
cus, without change of taste or appetite, the whole time.
Aphony. Fetid odor, she does not perceive it herself.
Coldness from the mouth to the stomach, immediately,
with nausea and inclination to vomit, a few hours after-
wards. Dryness of the mouth after its feeling cool, (5. d.)
Unusual dryness of mouth, before and after dinner; he is
frequently obliged to drink, (1. d.) Slimy mouth in the
morning, (3. d.) Swelling of the salivary and sub-maxil-
lary glands, with hardness and pain and increased secre-
tion of saliva. She gets easily choked when swallowing
anything.

Pharynx and (Esophagus.— Sore throat, day and night,

K1TRUM— NITRATE OP POTASH.

7

with inflammation of the velum pendulum palati and uvula,
for four day*, (a. 10 d.) Violent sore throat in the night,
as if the throat would close and she was not able to breathe.
Aching pain in the throat, as when inflammation com-
mences, for twenty-four hours, (a. 9 h ) Cutting sore
throat, apparently in the larynx, with impeded deglutition,
(a. 8 d.) Prickling pain in the throat, increased by deglu-
tition. Stitching in I he middle of the throat and fauces
during deglutition. Tilillation in the throat, he has to clear
the throat, but he does not throw off anything. Rough
throat (immediately.) Roughness and scraping sensation
in the throat ; she is frequently obliged to clear her throat,
which causes pain in the chest, evening and morning, (a.
8 d.) Roughness of the throat, with hoarseness and burn-
ing in the oesophagus, as in heart-burn. Hawking up of
mucus in the afternoon, sweetish and lough.

Taste and Appetite. — Repugnant tasle in the mouth,
the whole day, (a. 18 d.) Sour taste in the throat, in the
morning after rising. Sourish taste and increased accu-
mulation of saliva in the mouth, until after dinner, (3. d.)
Want of appetite with increased hunger, (2. d ) Dimin-
ished appetite, with distended abdomen, discharge of a
quantity of flatulence and tenesmus of the rectum. Di-
minished appetite. Good appetite, in spite of all pains, (a.
30 d.) Canine hunger, in the forenoon, every attack last-
irg a quarter of an hour, alternating with slight cutting
around the umbilicus. Thirst, without much appetite.
Thirsllessness, with good appetite, generally. Increase of
thirst, (a. 2 h.) Violent, continued thirst, (1. d.) Increase
of thirst, from morning till evening, (9. d.)

Gastric Symptoms. — Eructations, (1. d.) Frequent
eructations and nausea (immediately.) Hiccough, in the
morning, before breakfast, (14. d.) Heart-burn, (a. £ h.)
Heart-burn, and canine hunger, without much appetite, (a.
2 h.) Nausea, (8. d.) Nausea, with gulping up of mu-
cus. Nausea, with inclination to vomit, in the stomach
(shortly.) Nausea, with inclination to vomit, trembling of
the whole bodv, headache, as if bruised, choking sensation
in the throat, burning eyes, faintness, tearing and stitching
in the vertex and occiput, culling in the i itcslincs, and
finally expulsion of soft fasces, followed by mucus ; in tho

8

NITRUM — NITRATE OF POTASH.

evening, 9, 10 o'clock. Gulping-up of biltcr water, re-
lieving llie nausea, (a. 50 d.) Violent vomiting. Vomit-
ing, with taste of Nilrum, preceded by nausea (immedi-
ately.) Vomiting, first mucus and water, afterwards bloody
mucus. Violent vomiting. Bloody vomiting.

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Pain in the stomach. — Violent pain in the
slomach and whole body, (immediately.) Qualmishness
in the slomach, with accumulation of water in the mouth,
(during the menses.) Pressure in the stomach and colic,
without evacuation, from afternoon. till evening. Inclina-
tion to spasm of the stomach. Slight pressure and burn-
ing in the region of the stomach, gradually increasing to a
dull boring; half an hour afterwards cutting pain, follow-
ing the course of the intestines. Sharp, stitching pain in
the stomach and whole body, so violent that he was not
able to breathe without suffering the most intense pain.
Disagreeable sensation in the stomach, as if something in
the stomach would turn round. Pulsation in the region
of the orifice of the stomach. Feeling of coldness in the
slomach. Coldness and pain in the stomach, (immediately.)
Icy coldness in the stomach, painful to the touch ; going
off in the evening after lying down; accompanied by nau-
sea with inclination 1o vomit, and by gulping-up of water ;
the same symptom on the twentieth morning, after ealing
milk, but without inclination to vomit. Burning in the
stomach, with violent stilches in the region of the stomach,
(2. d.) Inflammation of the stomach. Aching pain in
the pit of the stomach. Pressure and gnawing in the pit
of the stomach, painful to the touch, (22. d.) Pressure in
the pit of the slomach, as if a button were pressing into
it, after dinner, (20. d.) Heaviness and fulness in the pit
of the stomach. Faintish weakness about the pit of the
stomach- Culling stitching in the pit of the slomach and
epigastrium, after breakfast. Pain in the left hypochon-
drium, as after a violent blow ; accompanied with pains in
the small of the back, which were frequently so violent
that she was unable to lie down, followed by leucorrhoea,
for eight days, ceasing together with the pain in the small
of the back, afier the menses. Stitcl ing in the region of
the left ribs, at regular intervals, after lifting a weight.
Colic. Violent colic, especially in the right side, after eat-

NlTIttJM NITRATE OF POTASH. *

ing veal, terminating in two hours in painful pressure at the
stomach, with a feeling of emptiness m the stomach ;
afterwards the colic returned in a few hours, and remained
the whole night, decreasing. Violent colic, followed by

men, evening. Distension and stitching in the left, side of

deeply ; if she attempts to breathe deeply, she is pre-

(4. d.) Painful sensation in the pit and region of

ration.0 Aching pain at the lower termination of the ster-
num, (a. 38 h.) Tensive pain across the chest, from after-
noon till evening, (1. d.) Stitches in the upper part of the

knuckles becoming distended and swollen ; thence the

ing in the right wrist-joint. Pain in the inner side of the

Breaking and tearing in the right hand, evening. Tear-

right hip when standing, going off during motion. Fre-
quent stitching and burning in the right hip, when at rest

General weariness and dulness in the lower limbs, after

days before die. menses,). (a. 22 d.) Tearing in the right

ness in the knee-joint, extending into the thigh, especially

ing in the ball of the sole of the left foot, in the evening,
(25. d.) Sudden, jerking tearing in the left sole, as in an

walking, (a. 20 d.) Tearing in the big loe of the" left
foot, (a. 10 d.) Jerking stitching in the right, big toe, in
the night. Stitches in the second toe of the left foot, at

the place which was formerly occupied by a corn. Painful
conlraciion of the iocs, in the evening when sitting.

General Symptoms and Fits. — Painless jerking in

day and night by a painful tearing, recurring at intervals,
and going off only for a short while by rubbing, (22. d.)
Formication in hands and feet ; afterwards in the tongue.
Convulsions. Swelling of the body, neck, thighs, so sud-
den that there is scarcely time left to open her dress.
Fainting fit with vertigo, in the morning when standing,

when the fit ceases, the pain goes down the lower limbs
into the ankles, where it remains seated the whole day ;
in the afternoon she feels cold, thirsty, more so when
in bed, until after midnight, when she fell asleep, feeling
an agreeable warmth. Fainting fit, at 10 o'clock in the
evening, (while blowing upon a musical instrument and
having tight clothes en ;) he felt as if all the things in the
room were turning round ; he was on the point of falling;
but, while falling, he made an effort and raised himself
again ; at the same time the interior of the head fell alter-
nately warm and cold, and he vacillated while standing,
with a feeling as if the fit would return. Paralysis of the
spinal marrow, with tetanus. Paralysis of the extremities.
Paralysis of the organs of sense. Death, (a. 36 h.) Chronic
cachexia. Death of a boy in two days, from six drachms.
Death, caused by one ounce. Fatal inflammation and
gangrene, from one ounce and a half, in the case of a

The majority of the symptoms occur in the
afternoon and evening. The symptoms which occur dining
the day, generally disappear in the evening after lying
down. She feels relieved when lying down, (a. 34 d.)
The pains grow worse when in bed. She feels less weak
when walking than when sitting. The syn ptoms, espe-
cially the headache, arc immediately relieved by smelling
of spirilus nitri dulcis. The symptoms grow worse by
smelling of camphor. Itching of several parts of the body,

19

also of the scalp ; she has sometimes 1o scratch the parts,
until they bleed, after which she sometimes feels a burning
pain. Itching, here and there, in the evening. Pricking,
followed by burning of the skin, especially in the face.
Small red spots on the neck and the left fore-arm, itching
when touching iho.m. Itching, especially of the thighs
and the parts covering the tibiae ; she has to scratch, until
blood comes, with small red spots here and ihere, (a. '20

(1. 2. d.) She felt at once so faint, worn out, and drowsy,

eyes ; she slumbered, and on waking, she was unable lo

Yawning, (1. d.) Drowsiness in day-time, also
when walking. Resllcss nights; frequently her sleep is

ravings which caused her to start and roused her from

Comatose sleep, as if she were intoxicated ; she
hears every thing which is spoken around her, (a. 6 d )
Sleep full of fancies ; ideas crowd upon her ; she is very
anxious. She falls asleep late in the night- Restless
sleep with frequent waking, (a. 10 d.) Restless night,
sleep rare and heavy. Restless night, until a slight sweat
breaks out in the morning. Feels very warm ; this hinders

Nightmare. Oppression of the chest from cough-
ing, in the night. Stitches under the right scapula in the
night. She dreamed she was travelling, but she did not
get along; this vexed her. Anxious, wild dreams during
the heat, with frequent, starlings and sweat; short chills in
the morning, and thirst in the forenoon, (a. 27 d.) She
dreams that she has a swollen check, or that her child is
beaten. She dreams that one of her teeth breaks off.
Dreams about danger, water, fire, etc. Dreams about

20

rows, vexation, disgust, dispute. She dreams she loses

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Feels immediately cool and fresh. Frequent
chilliness, in the afternoon. Violent chilliness, with trem-
bling of the whole body. Chi'ls in the forenoon, in the
open air, a quarter of an hour, without any subsequent
heat. Chilliness in the afternoon. Chilliness in the even-
ing, with a cold thrill over the back, going off when lying
down. Chilliness in the evening, going off when lying
clown, and recurring when rising, going off again alter
lying down, (during the menses.) Short chills, in the
evening. She feels cold in the evening, and cannot get
warm ; accompanied by headache, commencing at the ver-
tex. Chilliness in the open air, in the evening, with heat
in the face when in the room ; afterwards a general sweat.
Shuddering, in the evening, followed by flushes of heat,
and sweat after lying down, without any thirst, (9. d.)
Forehead and cheeks feel warmer, the hands being cool,
(a. 20 min.) Chilliness, heat, sweat, in alternation, in the
afternoon, (4. d.) Heat in the afternoon, followed by chil-
liness ; after lying down, in the evening, sweat with thirst,
until morning ; during the chilliness she has frequent
flushes of heat, and during the heat frequent chills; dur-
ing the sweats she had thrills of coldness as soon as she
uncovered herself, (ll.d.) Increased warmth in the trunk,
(a. 20 m.) Slight heat over the whole body, (a. i h.)
Heat and sweat over the whole body, no thirst, (in the

PETROLEUM— OLEUM PETRiE.

This product of the interior of the earth ought to be
fluid and light yellow, if it is to be used as a remedial
agent. Its smell, taste and medicinal virtues are very pow-
erful. When very fluid, it can scarcely be mixed with fat
vegetable oils. Nevertheless, in order to be quite sure of
its purity and genuineness, I have shown in my work en-
titled : Modes of ascertaining the genuineness and falsifi-
cation of remedial agents, (Dresden, 17s7, p. 221,) how
the purity of petroleum may be ascertained by adding
some strong sulphuric acid, which leaves the petroleum
untouched, acting merely upon the foreign oily matters and
converting them to a sort of sulphur. Or, if this testing
process appear too troublesome, a drop of petroleum may
be deposited on paper; if pure, it will soon evaporate in
the open air, without leaving a trace behind ; if not pure,
the trace of the foreign oily substance will be seen. In
many cases the petroleum may be found mixed with a vol-
atile, vegetable oil, the oil of turpentine for example. In
order to guard against this, it is well to mix the petroleum,
previous to its being used, with double its quantity of alco-
hol, to shake the mixture several times, and then to filter
it through blotting paper, which had been previously moist-
ened with alcohol. In this case the vegetable oil, if any was
present, is filtered through together with the alcohol, and
the pure petroleum remains behind, and ought to be pre-
served in a vial, the cork and mouth of which are to be her-
melically closed with sealing-wax. '

To make the first trituration, one drop of oil is used
instead of one grain of dry substances.

Petroleum has been especially efficacious in diseases
characterised by the following affections : —

Inflammation and swelling of the big toe, with pain.
Swelling of the toes. Itching in those toes which had
been frozen formerly (the first days.) White, painful
pimples between the toes. The corns are painful as if
pressed by tight shoes. Frequent and violent stitches in
the corns. Slinging burning in the corn, in wide shoes.
Painful inflammation of the corns.

General Symptoms. — When lying down, the limbs
immediately goto sleep. The limbs, arms, cervical mus-
cles, scalp, nates and feet go to sleep easily, especially when
lying down. Pressure in the upper and lower limbs, as if
they would go to sleep. Drawing pain in the limbs, in
the evening. Pushing in the limbs, almost like drawing.
A pain in the chest which was now over and had occurred
six weeks ago from a contusion, is felt again as an aching
pain, especially in the evening. Momentary drawing in
the knee, arm and shoulder. Tearing in the back, knees
and legs, in the evening when in bed. Sudden tearing or
jerking here and there in the body. Drawing pain in the
abdomen and in all the limbs, for hours in the arms, and
for whole days in the thighs. Violent drawing and tear-
ing through the knees and tibiae, especially in the evening.
The drawing (tearing) pains in the limbs become intolera-
ble when they are covered by feather beds. The pains
are relieved by external warmth, increased by coldness.
Most pains come on during rest and go off during motion.

SULPHUA. 30 i

The pains, especially those felt in the head and stomach,
come on in the open air when walking. The limbs feel
bruised, in the morning afier rising. Bone-pain of the
limbs, when feeling them, as if the flesh were detached.
She feels worst when standing. Cracking in the knees
and elbows. Pinching in the muscles here and there.
Uncomfortable sensation as if a!l the parts of the body

Weakness, Fits. — Single jerks of a hand and fool, in

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Cramp-like, uninterrupted yawning before bed-
time. Frequent yawning and stretching, without drowsi-
ness. A good deal of yavming and drowsiness the whole
day. Frequent yawning and cold hands. Unconquerable
drowsiness in the day. Drowsiness in the afternoon.
Very drowsy in the evening. Constant yawning in the
evening, for an hour, and an unconquerable weariness.
Long sleep in the morning. He sleeps much, and never-
theless does not feel refreshed in the morning. Has no
inclination whatsoever to rise in the morning. Is yet
drowsy at eight o'clock in the morning, with indisposition
to work. In the morning, sensation as if he had not slept
enough, with his eyes swollen, and with desire to stretch
himself. For many mornings he feels very lazy for "half
an hour, with pain in the back and lower limbs ; she had

SULPHUR. 305

to seat herself frequently. Deep sleep in the morning,
without any visible inspirations. Heat in the face and
nausea, in the morning when waking. Heaviness in the
back and lower limbs, in the morning when rising. She
feels very sleepy in the night, and her eye-lids feel heavy
and close ; nevertheless she is not able to fall asleep. She
does not full asleep under an hour, without any pain.
Difficulty of falling asleep, on accoum of ideas crowding
upon the mind. She frequently wakes from a sound sleep,
without any apparent cause. He wakes every half hour.
Wakeful the xohole night. He frequently wakes in the
night half, is however able- to think, and feels chilly. Sleep-
lessness, as if from nervous irritation. She does not
sleep at all, although she is tired. Tossing from side to
side in the bed, at night. He frequently turns to the other
side in the night, without waking. Great wakefulness in
the evening ; the blood rose to his head, and the night
was sleepless. Involuntary recollection, in the evening,
of a business which had been terminated. In the evening,
when performing some light work, she perspired for&a
short while, and dreamed afterwards that she had on a
dress which she ought to be very careful of, and guard
against stains. Talks loudly, while asleep, of the business
which he had done in the day-time. Restless night ; he
wakes xuith a start as if he hud had a fearful dream ; af-
ter waking he ivas yet full of anxious fancies, as of
ghosts, etc., of which he was not able to get rid. Sleep
full of dreams ; he wanders as if in delirium. She ima-
gines that she has seen or done the things she had merely
dreamed of. He imagined he heard a noise, in the even-
ing when on ihe point of dropping to sleep; this caused
mm to start so violently that the whole body felt it Fre-
quent starlings when asleep. Starting during the siesta.
Jerking with the foot, when slumbering. Violent head-
ache in the night, disturbing her rest. Waking in the
morning, with giddiness and dulness of the head He is
frequently roused in the night by a throbbing of the blood
in the head, afterwards in the chest. Violent palpitation
ot the heart in the night, when turning to the other side
IJigging-up sensation in the forehead, at night. Bnrniiiff
in the mouth at night, with thirst. Compressive pain in

306


the stomach, in the night after waking, going off by bend-
ing double. In the night, pressure at the stomach, for an
hour, relieved by eructations. At night, pressure at the
pit of the stomach, causing anxiety and accompanied by
palpitation of the heart ; several nights for hours. After
midnight, pressure at the stomach and throbbing headache.
Vertigo when waking in the night. Vertigo and nausea
in the night, while sweating ; every thing turned with her
until morning. Pain in the fore-teeth, in ihe night. Fre-
quent nausea in the night. About midnight, she is waked
by stitching and cutting in the abdomen. Nightly flatu-
lent colic, with retching, anguish and obtusion of the head.
At night, sharp stitches in the abdomen, followed by fre-
quent emissions of flatulence. At night, cramp-like pres-
sure in the abdomen. At night, contractive colic, all of a
sudden. Pressing in the abdomen from above downward,
it wakes her. Protrusion of the umbilical region, as if
caused by the uterus, in a pregnant female, at night, when
lying upon the back, in paroxysms of some minutes, (a.
14 d.) Sweat over the whole abdomen, at night, extend-
ing ns far as the groin, the feet being cold as far as the
ankles, and accompanied with dull cutting in the soles.
At night, during sleep, a humor and some faeces escaped
from her anus. Asthmatic in the evening when in bed.
Attacks of arrest of breathing, at night. Oppression of
the chest, in the night, as if the chest were oppressed by
a heavy load ; he had to sit up. He wakes in the morning
with rawness of the chest. At night, shocks in the left
chest towards the heart, arresting her breathine, with
great thirst, (a. 3 d.) Short and hacking cough for a
whole hour, in the evening after lying down ; this made
her feel hot ; again at three o'clock in the morning. San-
gineous expectoration at night, with greasy, sweetish taste
in the mouth. Quick beating of the heart, in the evening,
after turning from side to side for some time. Violent
pain in the' back for several nights, with bruised feeling
in the small of the back, and with great orgasm of the
blood. Violent pain in the hip-joint at night, also when
touched. Painless jerks in the small of the back, in the
evening when in bed. Aching pain in the thigh the whole
night. Tearing in the thigh and leg, at night when in bed,


307

she was not able to get warm in the bed. At night, he
is obliged to put his loiver limbs out of the bed to dimin-
ish the tearing. Tearing in both feet in the night, after
which they felt rigid and he was unable to sleep. Stitches
in the corns at night. Cramp in the calves when extend-
ing the feet. Heat of the feet, in the evening when in
bed, with a feeling of burning, obliging her to uncover
them several hours ; afterwards uneasiness, itching and
creeping in the feet. Titillation in the left upper and
lower limb, for two hours, in the evening; when in bed. A
good deal of stretching in the night. When sleeping, he
lays his arms over his head. Snoring. Palpitation of the
heart, at night. Sleeps with his eyes half open. Mutter-
ing. Sensation as if every part of his body trembled and
beat, at night when half awake. Great anxiety, in the
evening when in bed, (about full moon.) At night, he
wakes with great anguish and heat all over, and with sen-
sation of a spasmodic conditio,! in the body. Restless
sleep after midnight ; she dreams that she is having an at-
tack of fever' and wakes covered with sweat, with great
heat, especially in the face, thirst and chilly shuddering,
increasing by motion unto chattering of teeth. She ex-
claims, while sleeping, that she is black, etc. Exclama-
tions while asleep. Moaning while sleeping. Great heat
in the night, alternating with chilliness. He dreams he
has been bit by a dog. Anxious dreams, as if fire were
falling fronr Heaven. Anxious dream, as if he were being
oppressed and crushed by something, (nightmare.) Dreams
that he is falling from a height. Frightful dreams. Dis-
gusting dreams, with nausea when waking. Left the bed
the first three nights, like a somnambulist, saying : " My
head ! I am delirious !" and seized his forehead ; going off
after walking about. Anxious dream, during which she
leaves her bed unconsciously, followed by violent head-
ache, (a. 3, 4 d.) Anxious dream, before midnight ; she
rises, imagines that a fire has broken out, inquires at the
windows, and starts when perceiving that it is nothing but
a dream ; she felt bruised and faint for three days after.
Many vivid dreams. Ludicrous fancies before dropping
to sleep, in a sort of half dream, she laughed. For three
nights in succession he talked aloud of the things which he

308


saw in his fancy. Visions, as soon as he closes his eyes.
Horrid visions, as soon as she closes her eyes in the even-
ing. At night, when waking, an arithmetical figure was be-
fore her fancy, which gradually extended in size, until the
lines were half a foot wide. He fears he might catch cold
in the open air ; he knows not whether this is fancy or
physical reality.

Chilliness, followed by heat, in the evening
before falling asleep. Chilliness in the afternoon, after-
wards heat with thirst, cold feet and sweat in the face and
on the hands ; with dry night-cough, as soon as he gets
into bed. Creeping shuddering over the skin, without
chilliness. Passing chilliness, on the chest, arms and

Cold nose, hands and feet. Feeling of coldness
for several hours, without chilliness ; afterwards heat with
little thirst, slight sweat with headache and hoarseness,
great faintness and loss of appetite. Feeling of coldness
through all the limbs, without subsequent heat, in the fore-
noon. Chilliness in the back from below upward, in the
evening, for an hour, without subsequent heat. Frequent,
internal chilliness, without thirst. Chilliness in the night,
for four hours, preceded by colic, accompanied with heat
without sweat ; profuse sweat in the night following.
Chilliness every evening, which cannot be removed by the
warm stove ; great warmth in the bed, and sour sweat
every morning. Chilliness, with diarrhoea, for several
hours. Shaking chills in the evening, and great paleness
of the face. Shaking, feverish chilliness, frequently in the
evening. Shaking chilliness from seven to eight o'clock,
without thirst, with cold hands and violent pressure at the
stomach, as of a load ; afterwards the usual warmth, with
thirst. Chilliness and coldness of the whole body, after-
noon and evening. Chilliness from morning till evening.
Thrill of chilliness along the back ; it can be arrested by
the warmth of the stove. Chilliness, with thirst, even
near the stove, after dinner, until four o'clock. Chilli-
ness, and afterwards shaking over the whole body, com-
mencing at the toes, without heat or subsequent thirst, in
the afternoon. Chilliness with headache, in the evening;
going off after 'lying down. Constant thrill of chilliness
along the back, commencing in the small of the back,


309

in bed, with sweat and dryness in the throat. Heat to-

My co-observers are Fr. Hahnemann ; Franz ; Gross ;

Moral Symptoms.— Desponding, peevish mood. Melan-

she dreaded talking to any body. Sullen mood in the

absence of mind. Stupefaction.

Smarting, burning and running of the left eye, when read-

Bleeding of the nose, in the evening when sitting or

Urine like water. The urine becomes turbid when stand-

While' sediment in the urine. Brown-red urine. The

standing or sitting, obliging him to press the thighs against

Genital Organs. — Warmth in the genital organs and

testicles. Relaxation of the scrotum. Itching pain in
the upper border of the glans. Erections in the day-time,
without any amorous desires. Emission without any thrill.
Burning in the urethra, after an embrace. The woman
has a violent desire for an embrace, the desire being more
felt in the outer pudendum ; however, she is not much ex-
cited by the embrace. The female dreams twice that she
enjoys an emb-ace, and twice she discharges mucus from

an embrace ; when waking, she has a violent, furious de-
sire for an embrace, the desire being concentrated espe-
cially in the clitoris, (a. 40 h.) Sensaiion in the abdomen,
as if the menses would appear. Delays ihe menses by
eight days, without causing any troubJs. Menses loo late,
■with pain in the abdomen and small of the back. Menses
too early. Nightmare two days before the* menses ; sen-
sation as of a load lying upon her ; she was unable to talk,
sensation as if some one had strangulated her, she woke
in a perspiration. During the menses, stitches in the ab-
domen and vagina. Thirst and dry tongue during the
menses. After the menses great desire for an embrace,
(a. 1 1 d.) Great aversion to an embrace after the menses,
(a. 33 d.) Frequent discharge of corrosive mucus from
the vagina, (a. 16d.) Acrid, burning leucorrhcea. Trans-

Cold, Catarrh.— Unsuccessful desire to sneeze. A

stinate dry coryza; one or the other nostril being some-
times completely obstructed. Fluent coryza, (4 d.)

roughness m the larynx. Pain in the larynx, talking is

out expectorating ; a few hours after he throws off mucus

BARYTA CARBONICA.

Barium Carbonate. Ba Co 3.

In 1824 Stapf published in his Archives, Vol. Ill, No. 3, p. 183, the Baryta
ocetica, proved by himself and his friends Gross, Hartmann, Hartlaub Sen.,
Adams and Riickert Sen. There were two hundred and fifty-four symp-
toms, and some additional observations and collections of Hahnemann
on Baryta muriatica. Very few cures have since been published, notwith-
standing the masterly analysis of Stapf in his preface.

In 1828, in the first edition of " Chronic Diseases," Vol. II, p. 32, appeared
provings of Baryta carbonica, the symptoms numbering one hundred and
eight, which were united with the former of acetica, making in all two
hundred and eighty-six. In the second edition, in 1835, with the addition
of a second proving of Hartlaub and the numerous provings made on a
houseful of girls, by Nenning, and one proving of Eummel, the number of
symptoms increased to six hundred and eighteen. Neither Gross nor
Eiickert made a proving of the carbonica, the symptoms got in by mistake
of those who made the arrangement ; also Dr. Neumann's valuable ob-
servations., which were made after prescribing large doses of Baryta muri-
atica for two schoolboys, and corroborated by repetition. They found their
way even into Jahr's manuals, and all the repertories, from where they
have to be stricken.

As we have to deal here principally with the cured symptoms, and only
very few with Baryta acetica have been mentioned, Hahnemann's example
is followed, and both acetica and carbonica united, the former marked — .

This united collection will show that, great as the difference is from the
muriatica, there is hardly any between the two others, and certainly none
in the symptoms cured.

6. Face.— Face pale or yellowish, with sickly complexion ; and eyes
deep sunken, surrounded -by a blue circle. — Heat and burning sensation in
face, with deep redness of whole face, circumscribed redness of cheeks, or
else red spots, also on neck. — Pale or red swelling of face. — Swelling of
cheeks, with lancinating pain.-- Pain : tearing in r. half of face ; pressure on
malar bone and beneath eye ; stabbing below 1. zygoma with darting up side
of head. — Pain in all three divisions of fifth nerve (1.) ; from exposure to cold ;
draught of air ; worry ; beginning 5 p.m., lasts with slight intermissions three
or four days ; besides sharp dartings every few moments ; extreme external
sensitiveness. — Drawing, sharp pain, sensation as from a bruise, pressive and
burning sensation in cheek-bones. — Erysipelas of face (beginning on r. ear
and spreading over face). — Phlegmonous erysipelas in face, chiefly in eyelids,
nose, and (1.) ear. — Roughness and redness of skin of face. — Eruption of
pimples on face and on forehead. — Itching and moist tetters over whole face,
chiefly above nose, round eyes, and in eyehds ; small white vesicles in groups
and forming scabs. — Ephelides and black pores in face, chiefly on nose, lips,
and chin. — Lips dry, rough, and cracked. — Burning sensation and continued
heat of lips. — Yellowish hepatic spots on upper lip. — Tinea faciei. — ^Trembling
and jerking of lips. — Swelling of lips. — Swelling of lower lip with eruption on
it. — Scabious ulcer on red of lip.— -Cancer of the lips. — Herpetic eruption in
corner of mouth. — Painful eruption round chin. — Sharp, lancinating, and
drawing pains, and painful swelling in jaws. — Swelling of submaxillary glands,
with pains and lancinations when touched.

7. Teeth. — Great tenderness of teeth. — Great sensitiveness of points of
teetfcu — ^Jerking, shocks, sharp or drawing pains ; shootings ; throbbing pains ;
boring and burning sensation, both in carious and in sound teeth. — ^Tearing
toothache on 1. side.— Pulsation and boring in teeth, < from heat — ^The
toothache often extends as far as ears or into head, and is sometimes accom-
panied by congestion of blood in head, with shiverings and disposition to
sleep, or with swelling of cheek. — ^Appearance or < of toothache, prin-
cipally in evening ; at night ; or in open air ; also from a current of air ; from
cold water ; when masticating, and sometimes when taking anything hot —
Toothache with congestions to head, or stitches in ears. — Brownish mucus on

8. Mouth. — Dryness, heat, and burning sensation in mouth, some-
times in morning with moist tongue. — Great dryness of palate with much
thirst ; obliged to drink much. — Mouth dry, insipid, and sticky in morning.
— PtyaUsm from abuse of Mercury or during a fever. — ^Accumulation of
saliva in mouth : sanguineous ; salt ; acid ; bitter ; or mixed with blood ;
even after eating. — Fetid, sometimes acid, smell from mouth, esp. in
morning or in evening or after a meal. — ^Vesicles, blisters, and aphthae in
mouth and on tongue, sometimes with burning, or with pain of excoriation,
when eating. — Exfoliation of membrane of mouth. — Burning sensation and
tickhng on tongue. — Pain, swelling, and inflammation of tongue for three
days. — Tongue dry, rough, and cracked, of colour of cinnabar; or loaded
with a white coating, or covered with brownish, thick, and viscid mucus. —

Stottering when speaking.-^Accumulatioo of saltish mucus in mouth.— Taste :
bitter ; pasty ; offensive ; of blood ; sweetish ; metallic — ^Bilious taste in
mouth when fasting ; though food tastes right— Bitter taste with dulness
of head and ill-humour.— *Acid taste all day.

Q. Throat. — Scraping, roughness (rawness), and dryness in throat
(hawking and clearing throat). — Pressure as from a plug or from a tumour iii
throat, sometimes with difficult deglutition. — Stitches in throat on swallowing.
— Sensation as if a hard ball were ascending throat, and would close pharynx
and take away the breath.— Contraction and painful sensation of constriction
in throat when swallowing.^Sensation of contraction in throat — R. T. C.)
— Dryness of throat — Pain as from excoriation, burning sensation and shoot-
ings in throat, < during empty deglutition (soreness begins on r. side and goes
to 1. ; redness of tonsils). — Burning in throat as from sour eructations. —
Sensation during empty deglutition as of swallowing a piece of meat — Sen-

swelling of glands of neck. — Elongation of palate ; swelling of palate and
tonsils. — Sensation of a hair in throat — ^Angina gangrenosa.

10. Appetite. — Bad taste in mouth, mostly acid, bitter, or putrid and
sweetish or mawkish, < in morning on waking. — ^Taste bitter or too salt or
insipidity of food. — Complete anorexia and dislike to food, principally to
meat, rye bread, fat, and milk. — Dislike to sweet and acid things, or craving

desire for beer. — Craving (in drunkards) for wine and brandy. — Immoderate
appetite and attacks of bulimy, sometimes with headache, lassitude, and want
to he down. — Ravenous hunger which obliges him to eat frequently, gets
headache and has to lie down if he does not — Hungry, but appetite vanishes
at sight of food, feels full in abdomen ; when he begins tp eat is averse to it
— Desire for sweets.-^-Complaints from eating sweets. — ^Complaints from
farinaceous food. — Desire for raw food. — Great weakness of digestion, prin-
cipally for meat, fat, milk, acids, and farinaceous food, all of which some-
times cause great suffering, — Food sweetened with sugar < the pains in the
stomach and abdomen. — Milk produces sour risings, an acid taste in mouth,
and even vomiting. — Beer is followed by a prolonged after-taste, and causes
ebullition of blood. — Disgust for drinking wine. — ^After a meal oppression
in chest, nausea, pressure, and cramps in stomach, colic, inflation of abdomen,
flatulence, vomiting, great fatigue, shivering, confusion and pain in head, heat
in face, burning sensation in hands, flow of water from mouth, and many
other sufferings.

iz. Stomach. — Continued eructations, principally empty, or with taste

wards. — Movement and digging in abdomen, or sensation as if something
were pushed outwards. — Movements in abdomen as of the fist of a child. —
Pains as from contusion and bruising in integuments of abdomen. — Painful

13. Stool and Anus. — Constipation, and hard, knotty, and insufficient
evacuations. — Frequent and often ineffectual want to evacuate, chiefly at
night, and sometimes with pressure on rectum and bladder and pain in anus.
— Urgent want to evacuate. — Looseness of bowels; redness about anus;
obstructed evacuation, particularly if hard stools are retained. — Diarrhoea,
particularly where there is the red line about the anus, and the patient can't
wait, must go immediately desire is felt ; also waking early in morning with
diarrhoea, which drives one out of bed in a great hurry ; tenesmus in the
same way, drives one in a great hurry ; rumbling and rolling in bowels. —
Cholera asiatica ; as prophylactic, a pinch of the powdered milk of Sulphur
worn in stockings in contact with soles of feet; diarrhoea commencing
between midnight and morning, vomiting at same time ; numbness of limbs,
cramp in calves and soles, blue under eyes, cold skin, indifference ; during
convalescence, red spots, furuncles, &c. ; susceptibility to temperature, warm
things feel hot ; nerve symptoms (Hering). — Diarrhoea with frequent evacua-
tions, chiefly at night, and often with colic, tenesmus, inflation of abdomen,
dyspnoea, shivering, and weakness to the extent of fainting. — Evacuations :
mucous, watery, frothy, or acid, or of a putrid smell, or of undigested sub-
stances.— Stools : nearly black, loose, viscid, greasy, with pungent odour of
sulphuretted hydrogen. — Stool hard, as if burnt. — Stool, with sensation as if
some remained, and as if the stool had been insufiicient. — Discharge of liquid
from anus, followed by faeces at night during sleep. — Diarrhoea : painless ; in
morning compelling one to rise from bed (at 5 a.m., one stool an hour till
9 a.m.) ; undigested, involuntary ; diarrhoea in children, green, of bloody
mucus, with crying and weeping. — Dysenteric stools at night, with colic and
violent tenesmus. — Colic before every loose evacuation. — During stool, dis-
charge of blood ; pain in small of back ; palpitation of heart ; congestion of
head; itching, burning, and stinging at anus and in rectum. — ^After stool
tenesmus, constriction at anus. — Whitish, greenish, discoloured, or brownish-
red fasces. — Involuntary evacuations (when sneezing or laughing, with emis-
sion of flatus). — Evacuations mingled with mucus, blood, and purulent matter.
— Discharge of mucus, even with hard faeces. — Ejection of lumbrici, ascarides,
and also of pieces of taenia from rectum. — Prolapsus recti, esp. when evacuat-
ing (a hard stool). — Sharp and pressive pains, itching, shootings, stitches, and
burning in anus and rectum, even when not at stool. — Burning in anus,
before, during, and after stool. — Prostration follows stool.-^DuU ache just
inside coccyx, awful dead ache as if the heart would stop. — ^All pains seem to
go to rectum, life-taking pains. — Blind piles with burning as if something
were biting at anus, going away when l3ring down, coming on when standing
or walking about (produced. — R. T. C). — Haemorrhoids which protrude, ooze
and bleed. — Anus inflamed, swollen, covered with red veins. — Excoriation
and swelling of anus. — Much itching about anus; itching runs back along
perinaeum and adjacent parts. — Involuntary discharge of moisture from anus,
with itching in it. — Suppressed haemorrhoids, with colic, palpitation, conges-
tion to lungs ; back feels stiff as if bruised. — Constant bearing down towards
anus ; forcing down after sitting.

14. Urinary Organs.— Violent pain in region of kidneys after stooping

parts. — Redness and inflammation of orifice of urethra, and pain as at com-
mencement of gonorrhoea. — Discharge of mucus from urethra. — Haemorrhage

and inguina.

15. Male Sexual Organs. — ^Aflections of the genitals in general —
Itching about genitals on going to bed at night. — Fetid perspiration in parts.
— Excoriation between thighs and in groins, chiefly when waUdng. — Shootings
in penis and glans. — Prepuce stiff, hard, like leather, with copious secretion of
fetid smegma. — Inflammation, swelling, and phimosis of prepuce (with dis-
charge of fetid pus), with deep cracks, burning, and redness. — Deep (suppu-
rating) ulcer with elevated margins in glans and prepuce (with putfed edges).
— ^Aching, tension, and shootings in testes and spermatic cords.--*-Swelling and
thickening of epididymis. — Excoriation and oozing in scrotum. — Increased
sexual desire and voluptuous irritation of the parts, often without erection. —
Weakness of the genital functions, often with icy coldness, bluish colour of
glans, prepuce, and penis, and retraction of prepuce. — ^Testes relaxed and
hanging down. — Hydrocele. — Frequent pollutions, also at noon. — Watery
semen. — Involimtary discharge of semen, with burning in urethra. — ^Too
quick discharge of semen during coition. — Escape of prostatic fluid, chiefly
when urinating and while at stool. — Impotence.-H(Induration of testes.)

16. Female Sexual Organs. — ^A weak feeling in genitals. — Sore
feeling in vagina during an embrace. — Labour-like pain over symphysis. —
Uterine pains running from groins to back. — Moroseness and apprehension
with uterine pain. — Pressure on the parts. — (Bearing down with nightly
enuresis. — R. T. C.) — Excoriation, troublesome itching and burning sensation
in genitals; with papular eruption around them. — Burning in the vagina;
is scarcely able to keep still. — ^Ascarides of vulva. — Inflammation of labia.
— Menses too late ; too short. — Delay of first menses. — (Amenorrhcea, dread-
ful depression and apprehension, head feels full and heavy, followed by
violent headache, numbness of arms and legs, cramp and sick feeling

at molimen. — R, T, C.) — (Imperfect development of the genital organs,
menstruation does not appear at the usual age; breasts imperfectly
developed; pains about the shoulders, in the stomach after meals, in
1. side on inspiration; anorexia and vertigo. — R. T. C.) — Catamenia pre-
mature and too profuse; or too feeble or entirely suppressed (particularly
in psoric individuals), with colic, abdominal spasms, headache, pains in
loins, pressure at stomach, congestion in head, and nasal haemorrhage,
agitation, and even attacks of epilepsy. — Menstrual blood thick, acrid,
corroding thighs ; scanty, dark ; dark, putrid, clotted. — Before menses :
headache, itching in the parts ; spasmodic colic ; inquietude ; cough ; tooth-
ache; pyrosis; epistaxis; leucorrhoea, and asthmatic sufferings. — Bearing
down in pelvis ; congestion to uterus.— Sterility, with too early and profuse
menstruation. — Prolapsus : from reaching high ; with pain in hypogastrium,
esp. r. side ; with metritis ; with dropsy of uterus. — Promotes expulsion of
moles. — Morning sickness of pregnancy not amounting to vomiting, faint,
^ckish spells forenoon, profuse salivation, taste of which =s nausea ; aversion
to meat ; craves beer or brandy. — Haemorrhoids during pregnancy and in
childbed. — ^After menses : itching in nose. — Menstrual blood too pale or of an
acid smetL — Leucorrhcea sometimes corrosive ; gnawing and yellowish, pre-
ceded by colic. — Cancer of uterus ; offensive, corrosive, ichorous leucorrhcea ;
sensation of heat in crown of head ; coldness of feet ; flushes of heat pass off
in a perspiration with faintness ; weak at pit of stomach zi a.m. to 12 ; violent
burning in vagina, with painful soreness during coitus. — Hot flushes at
climaxis, with hot head, hands, and feet, and great goneness in stomach. —
Excoriation and itching in nipples. — ^Cracks in nipples, with burning sensa-
tion, easily bleeding, and ulceration (the nipple smarts and burns very much
as soon as the infant lets go of it). — Mammary glands engorged and inflamed.
— Erysipelatous inflammation of mammae ; they are hard, with red rays
extending from nipple, and stitching pains. — Swelling of mammae. — Nodo-
sities in mammae.— -Scirrhus of breast.

17. Respiratory Organs. — Catarrh, with fluent coryza, cough, pain in
chest, as if it were raw, and shivering. — Hoarseness, evening and morning,
roughness, and scraping in throat, with accumulation of mucus in chest. —
Pain as from excoriation, and tingling or tickling in larynx, with tendency to
cough. — Coldness in throat during an inspiration. — ^Voice hoarse and low, or en-
tirely extinct, generally in cold and damp weather. — Sensation as if larynx were
swollen, or as if a foreign body were in it. — Short, dry cough. — Dry cough, some-
times fatiguing and shaking, with retching, vomiting, and spasmodic constriction
of chest, esp. in evening, or at night, in a recumbent position, or in morning,
or after a meal. — (Constant cough with irritation of throat and wheezing.
— ^R. T. C.) — Moist cough, with profuse expectoration of thick, whitish, or

Gharaotaristios. — Sul. h. is a colourless, inflammable gas, having
a sweetish taste and an exceedingly fetid smell resembling rotten eggs.
It is extremely poisonous when inhaled. It is evolved when animal
or vegetable tissues containing Sulphur decays ; and it also occurs in
mineral springs, being liberated by the reduction of gypsum or other
sulphates through the action of a microbe (Cent, Diet). SuL h. is one
of the agents which give rise to " blood p)oisoning " when bad smells
are encountered. Asphyxia, tetanus, delirium, low continued fever
have been observed as resulting from the gas. J. Wiglesworth
(B.A/.y,, July i6, 1892) has recorded two cases of insanity, one
certainly, and both probably, due to inhaling the gas : R. H., 32,
engineman at chemical works, bad been kept at home with an
attack of bronchitis for ten days. A few days after his return to work
he became " gassed " (t .^., accidentally inhaled Sul, A.). This caused
headache, stupor, prostration, compelling him to stay at home for a
few days, when he t>ecame wildly delirious. He passed rapidly into
a very excited state, shouting and gesticulating ; said he was Jesus
Christ, &c. ; tried to bury his head in the floor and to raise his feet
above his head. Three days later he was admitted to Rainhill Asylum,
and was there still very violent and excited, gesticulating and talking
incoherently, chiefly on religious subjects. At the end of a month
there was some improvement, and he was discharged, recovered,
five months sdfter admission. In the other case, that of a labourer at
chemical works, Wiglesworth is not quite certain that Sul. K was
the poison inhaled. This patient was greatly excited ; threw his
arms about ; shouted and laughed by turns ; was excited and talka-
tive. He remained permanently insane.
